A0233.title: Swarm Coordination Fault Tolerance & Byzantine Defense
keywords: swarm coordination fault tolerance & byzantine defense
A0233.definition: Swarm communication redundancy, byzantine fault-tolerant consensus, member-behavior anomaly detection and isolation, and swarm-level e-stop and degraded operation to prevent individual hijacked or faulty members from causing whole-swarm loss-of-control.
A0233.description: Cluster cooperative fault tolerance and Byzantine defense targets the risk of cascading loss of control in multi-robot clusters caused by individual members being hijacked as Byzantine nodes, communication interruptions, or algorithmic flaws, and constructs a four-layer defense. First, communication redundancy: multi-path communication among cluster members ensures that a single link failure does not cause consensus failure. Second, Byzantine fault-tolerant consensus (e.g., PBFT, HoneyBadger): correct consensus can still be reached even when some members send erroneous information. Third, member behavioral anomaly detection: members that deviate from the cluster protocol (e.g., sending abnormal commands, trajectory deviation) are identified and isolated. Fourth, cluster-level emergency stop and degraded operation: when cluster loss of control is detected, all members perform an emergency stop or degrade to a safe mode. This measure is the core defense after loss-of-control scenarios in KARGU-2 autonomous weapons, warehouse AMR clusters, etc., and cooperates with A0232 (robot safety stop E-stop and functional safety design) and A0108 (IoT device network isolation and access control), where the former manages single-unit shutdown and this measure manages cluster-level cooperative fault tolerance.
A0233.limitation: Byzantine fault tolerance increases communication and computation overhead, leading to high consensus latency in large-scale clusters that is difficult to meet real-time control requirements. False positives in anomaly detection can cause normal members to be mistakenly isolated. Cluster-level emergency stop may be exploited by attackers to launch denial-of-service attacks. Defense fails when the number of members exceeds the fault tolerance threshold.
